extraPins.name: George C. Marshall
extraPins.caption: “Yes, evidently that is George C. Marshall stood at the base of the hill. Awkwardly out of the way, why is he here?”

extraPins.name: Peter Jansen Wessel (Tordenskiold)
extraPins.caption: “Certainly a man that gives off pirate energy”

extraPins.name: Scuba diver statue
extraPins.caption: “This statue sits ready to plunge into the water at any moment. It’s simply perfect for the pier”

extraPins.name: Untuned Bell
extraPins.caption: “Very, very easy to miss at first. You can control the bell with a pedal on the ground.”

extraPins.name: Rådhusplassen
extraPins.caption: “This pier is where you’ll catch some of the boat tours of the fjords. It’s also the back side of the stunning City Hall building, which has a nice view of the water. There’s also a number of statues around the area.”

extraPins.name: Oslo City Hall
extraPins.caption: “Despite City Hall being closed when I visited, the building is just spectacular, and still well worth visiting. Each face is unique, with the best faces being the one from the water, and the one with the clock, in my opinion.”

extraPins.name: Nordraaks plass
extraPins.caption: “Absolutely one of the coolest small parks in the city, if not the whole Nordics. There are giant dragon statues, chained up for our protection.”

extraPins.name: Dronning Sonja
extraPins.caption: “For the Royal Funeral, all of the Royal statues across the country had flowers placed on them, but I don’t think anyone got more than Dronning Sonja. She was absolutely covered.”

extraPins.name: Dronning Maud
extraPins.caption: “Not quite the most prominently featured statue in the Slottenspark, but Maud is located in one of the nicer wooded areas. Maud is depicted in the typical Norwegian style here.”

extraPins.name: Karl Johan Monument
extraPins.caption: “Karl Johan sits high on his horse, towering above on a pedestal, facing the Palace. At the time of the Royal Funeral, the whole area was covered in flowers and flags in respect to the late King. …”

extraPins.name: The Royal Palace
extraPins.caption: “Though the Palace is currently closed, there are still ceremonies held on the Palace grounds, which are open to the public. The Royal Funeral was held here, and the King lied in wake for a period prior.”

extraPins.name: Slottsparken
extraPins.caption: “Slottsparken is the multiblock-sized park that surrounds the royal palace. There’s a pathway which has a series of modern art items along it, and a few more lined by trees. Royal ceremonies are held here, including the recent Royal Funeral (pictured)”

extraPins.name: Aanerud Bakeri Oslo
extraPins.caption: “A small, lovely bakery. Aanerud Bakeri is located down a side street, a bit outside of downtown. The pastries were fantastic, you can skip the drip coffee.”

extraPins.name: Martin Place
extraPins.caption: “Sydney’s central business district is littered with giant, majestic, parliament-style buildings, and Martin Place is one of this set. Just stunning on its own, but somehow out of place in its current home”

extraPins.name: K H A O • S O I - カ オ • ソ ー イ
extraPins.location: Level 2/73-75 Liverpool St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
extraPins.caption: “I love Khao Soi, it’s one of my favorite Thai dishes. I’ve been to Chiang Mai, in northern Thailand, where the dish comes from. While the Khao Soi here was fine, it was quite unique in a way that I didn’t love. I’ve never had one so spicy. I often love spice, but with Khao Soi’s pickled taste profile, it just wasn’t my favorite combo.”

extraPins.name: Hyatt Regency Sydney
extraPins.caption: “Set right on Cockle Bay, the Hyatt Regency is a very nice business hotel. I’ve stayed here twice, and both times the rooms were quite large and well stocked. As always, I prefer a usable mini-fridge to one that’s trying to sell me products.”

extraPins.name: AG LEGO® Certified Store Sydney, Pitt St Mall – World’s Largest LEGO® Certified Store
extraPins.location: entry is Via, 400 George Street, Pitt Street Mall, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
extraPins.caption: “This store claims to be the largest LEGO store in the world, and I find that a bit surprising, but sure it’s quite sizable and has a lot of the iconic brick company’s partnerships on display. It’s a fun place to stop while exploring the capital’s downtown.”

extraPins.name: Royal Clock
extraPins.caption: “Queen Victoria Building has two impressive clocks, and the Royal Clock is the bulkier, more castle-resembling one. It’s got its charm, don’t get me wrong, but it’s definitely the lesser of the pair.”

extraPins.name: Great Australian Clock
extraPins.caption: “There are two tiered clocks hanging from Queen Victoria Building and the Great Australian Clock appears to tell the story of the country/continent. The clock has so many details, the longer you inspect it, the more you get from it”

extraPins.name: Queen Victoria Building
extraPins.caption: “The central business district of Syndey has a number of stunning, imperial buildings, and the Queen Victory stands alone as the singular best. From the glass panel on the windows, to the two giant, ornate clocks that hang in either hall, to the historical note in the top floor, this mall has a lot to see apart from the modern day stores.”

extraPins.name: Athena
extraPins.caption: “Small, simple, and elegant, I really enjoyed this statue, and found its existence additive to the city’s beauty”

extraPins.name: The Strand Arcade
extraPins.caption: “Sydney’s downtown should be known for its stunning buildings, and The Strand Arcade, one of many similar arcades, stands near the very top of the class. A tall, straight, singular hall with colorful, slanted, angular panels on the roof, and red carpeting and accenting provide a wonderful visual.”

extraPins.name: Sydney Arcade
extraPins.caption: “There’s a few arcades (in the British sense, meaning a long covered building) in Sydney, but the eponymous one is definitely not the top one. Potentially the LEGO store is the most notable thing about this building, apart from the lovely building itself.”

extraPins.name: Cenotaph
extraPins.caption: “Quite the beautiful monument, one of many in this area, which has an entire pedestrian-only street devoted to it. There were plentiful fresh wreaths when I visited, the area was extremely well kept”

extraPins.name: Royal Australian Regiment Memorial
extraPins.location: Regimental Square, 339A George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
extraPins.caption: “Not a giant monument, in stature, but still an impactful one. You’re just walking around the central business district and suddenly you stumble upon it”

extraPins.name: Rabbit woman, Dogman, vespa and coffee
extraPins.location: Australia Square, 264 George St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
extraPins.caption: “A lovely statue, a part of a series located in major cities around the work. It does appear that Rabbitwoman was originally holding something (maybe a coffee cup) which is now gone.”

extraPins.name: Sirius Cannon
extraPins.caption: “This is actually a display in two parts: first the more obvious anchor, which is set off the ground, and then the cannon placed outwards, almost to intimidate oneself not to speak ill of the mediocre anchor”

extraPins.name: Sirius Anchor
extraPins.caption: “Quite the large anchor is affixed onto a bit of ground, which itself is presented as a bit of art. Nah”

extraPins.name: Thomas Sutcliff Mort
extraPins.caption: “Ol Tom is situated way up high, leaning on something of a pedestal as he gazes down on the masses”

extraPins.name: Obelisk of Distances
extraPins.caption: “This obelisk almost taunts the reader in saying, “I bet you can’t make it to all of these far off locations”. And one day I hope to return to prove this monument wrong”

extraPins.name: Principal Road Marker
extraPins.caption: “It’s a fine obelisk, and truly one of the finer monuments in Macquarie Place Park, but does an obelisk evoke roads? Maybe it’s a literal representation of a road”

extraPins.name: Macquarie Place Park
extraPins.caption: “A very small park, but it rises above its smaller stature by being jam packed full of monuments, each fairly interesting in its own regard.”

extraPins.name: Bonds of Friendship
extraPins.caption: “I did knot get this piece of art”

extraPins.name: Second World War Servicewomen Memorial
extraPins.location: Jessie Street Gardens, 1-29 Loftus St, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
extraPins.caption: “A statue recognizing the unsung and so oft unrecognized heroes of the second world war.”

extraPins.name: Jessie Street Gardens
extraPins.caption: “The tiniest of greeneries, set entirely between giant skyscrapers, and filled with monuments. Jessie Street Gardens is many things, but hardly a garden (in the American sense)”

extraPins.name: Moore Steps
extraPins.caption: “One of the staircases that’ll get you down to the water portion of Circular Quay. Nothing spectacular but it does get the job done.”

extraPins.name: Circular Quay Wharf
extraPins.caption: “The main waterfront area with the Opera House. It’s a great place to get some photos taken. Also, look down, as there’s a series of writers featured in little circles”

extraPins.name: Trader’s Grill
extraPins.caption: “Trader’s Grill is the restaurant within The Explorer Hotel, and it’s one of the nicest restaurants in Yellowknife. The Grilled Bison Ribeye was delicious and came with some nice sides. They also have Ice Wine for dessert. Trader’s has a …”

extraPins.name: The Explorer Hotel
extraPins.caption: “I spent a single night at The Explorer Hotel, but I would stay long if I were in town for longer as everything was great: the restaurant, the rooms, the polar bear in the lobby - all of the essentials.”

extraPins.name: Bristol Monument
extraPins.location: 361 Old Airport Rd, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T2, Canada
extraPins.caption: “One of the first things to greet you when you arrive in Yellowknife, the Bristol Monument sits high atop a hill above the welcome sign, with a brilliant and bright blue and red accented plane”

extraPins.name: welcome yellowknife sign
extraPins.caption: “The Welcome Sign itself is pretty impressive, with the yellow knife and block text, how that pales in comparison to the large plane situated atop the hill next to it. All-in-all, this makes for one compelling stop”

extraPins.name: Lakeshore Co-op Gas Bar
extraPins.location: 321 Old Airport Rd, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T3, Canada
extraPins.caption: “This Co-op is located decently close to the airport if you’re returning a rental car. The shop is very well stocked”

extraPins.name: Woodcutter's Monument
extraPins.caption: “Absolutely nothing to see in March, and a bit annoying to get to. Skip this one outside of summer”

extraPins.name: Welcome to Fort Smith Sign
extraPins.location: McDougal Rd, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
extraPins.caption: “A fine looking sign, for sure. People in town recommend coming out here, or to the airport, to get good pictures of the northern lights”

extraPins.name: Tim Hortons
extraPins.location: 50 Trout St, Fort Smith, NT X0E 0A4, Canada
extraPins.caption: “Definitely the most remote Tim Hortons that I’ve visited. And on account of that remoteness, the selection is a bit more limited here than at some of the locations down south. If you show up in the mornings, there’s something of a line, but it moves fast.”

extraPins.name: Hay River Public Beach
extraPins.caption: “I came here to watch a sunrise in March, and it was -39°, the coldest temperature that I felt in the subarctic. It’s a nice place to take in the rising winter sun, but it can get seriously cold here, being exposed to the lake air.”

extraPins.name: Hay River Inukshuk
extraPins.location: 73 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
extraPins.caption: “The Inukshuk is stood in front of the Fire Department, between the Canadian and Northwestern Territories flags, looking imposing as you drive into downtown Hay River. Quite a sight to behold”

extraPins.name: Hay River Fire Department
extraPins.location: 73 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 1G2, Canada
extraPins.caption: “One of the more beautiful structures in Hay River, especially at dusk”

extraPins.name: Northmart
extraPins.location: 81 Woodland Dr, Hay River, NT X0E 0R3, Canada
extraPins.caption: “A very large store, in the historic and general sense, which has whatever you need. My main complaint is how early they close (6pm) as there were multiple times when I wanted a late night snack to no avail”

extraPins.name: Doghouse pub
extraPins.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
extraPins.caption: “I visited the Keys Lounge a few times before I decided to try the Doghouse Pub (they share a menu, including the bar options), and wow, as a solo diner I had a much better time eating at the bar. If you’re planning to eat alone, go in the back entrance and eat in The Doghouse at the bar.”

extraPins.name: Keys Dining Lounge & Restaurant
extraPins.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
extraPins.caption: “Keys Dining Lounge is located within the Ptarmigan Inn, and is most likely the nicest restaurant within 3hrs of Hay River. I came here a few times and really enjoyed the Poutine, Ribs, Wings, and the Burger (which also supports charity). …”

extraPins.name: Ptarmigan Inn
extraPins.location: 10 J Gagnier Rd, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
extraPins.caption: “Whether you’re staying at the Ptarmigan Inn or not, they have one of the best restaurants in town (Keys Lounge) and one of the best bars in the surrounding 6hrs (Doghouse Pub). It’s a nice place to stop while you’re in town”

extraPins.name: Ring's Pharmacy Ltd
extraPins.location: 6 Courtoreille St, Hay River, NT X0E 0A9, Canada
extraPins.caption: “A fairly full pharmacy and convenience store for the remoteness of the region”

extraPins.name: Town of Hay River
extraPins.location: 62 Woodland Dr #100, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
extraPins.caption: “While it doesn’t necessarily have the best reputation among locals across the NWT, I enjoyed my days in Hay River. There’s a few hotels, a couple good restaurants, a coffee shop, and everything else you need to survive up here. Hay River is a fine place to visit”

extraPins.name: Cambridge Executive Suites
extraPins.location: 31 Capital Dr #101, Hay River, NT X0E 1G1, Canada
extraPins.caption: “I really did enjoy staying at the Cambridge Executive Suites, and like the people that own it, but when they only clean with a broom and dustpan, they leave a lot of hair in the rooms. Otherwise, the apartments are wonderful, but they need to invest in a vacuum”

extraPins.name: Town welcome sign
extraPins.location: Q5VJ+8C, Hay River, NT X0E 1G5, Canada
extraPins.caption: “Hey, it is a beautiful sign. You wanna stop and take it in on the way into town.”

extraPins.name: Miss Saigon
extraPins.location: Inside Kim’s Confectionary, 5309 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1E3, Canada
extraPins.caption: “Miss Saigon is an absolutely delicious takeout option just a few blocks outside of downtown Yellowknife. Located inside of Kim’s Confectionery, this unassuming location doesn’t have the best aesthetics, but makes some delicious Vietnamese food with great portions for a low cost”

extraPins.name: Kim's Confectionary
extraPins.location: 5309 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P1, Canada
extraPins.caption: “A slightly smaller convenience store, but they carry a variety of more snacky options, and a few more packaged staples. Miss Saigon’s is located inside of Kim’s, and is great!”

extraPins.name: Dettah Ice Road
extraPins.location: School Draw Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3G2, Canada
extraPins.caption: “It’s less of a singular road (at the Yellowknife portion) and more of a, people drive on the lake to go where they need to. Multiple entrances and multiple exits, but with one major artery heading further into the lake.”

extraPins.name: Snowkings' Winter Festival
extraPins.location: 1 Kingsway, Yellowknife Bay, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P2, Canada
extraPins.caption: “This year was the 31st anniversary of Snowkings’ Winter Festival, in which they build an expansive ice castle on the frozen lake, with an ice carving contest situated outside. It’s a truly impressive endeavor, executed to an excellent …”

extraPins.name: Gallery of the Midnight Sun
extraPins.location: 5005 Bryson Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2A3, Canada
extraPins.caption: “A gallery with a variety of local crafts and taxidermies, including a number of beautiful, more premium art pieces. It’s nice to walk through this gallery regardless of whether you intend to buy anything.”

extraPins.name: Down to Earth Gallery
extraPins.location: 5007 Bryson Dr, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2A3, Canada
extraPins.caption: “A lovely little gallery and local craft and art shop, which is packed full of goodies. The location is located inside of a log cabin ordained with local art”

extraPins.name: NWT Brewing Company / The Woodyard Brewhouse & Eatery
extraPins.location: 3905 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2S6, Canada
extraPins.caption: “If you have some spare time in Yellowknife, plop yourself down at the bar at NWT Brewing and you’ll discover a number of great local beers, and equally great local people. They brew a beer each year for the Snowkings Ice Festival, on the lake next door, each winter.”

extraPins.name: Aurora Emporium Art Gallery
extraPins.location: 4701 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 2P1, Canada
extraPins.caption: “The owner is a longtime Yellowknifer who sells a number of local crafts, perfect for gifts down south. They’ll also print your pictures on mugs, especially ones of northern lights.”

extraPins.name: Centre Square Mall
extraPins.caption: “One of the most prominent buildings in downtown Yellowknife, and while it may not be as thriving as it once was, evidenced by a lot of people standing around and a whole section being closed off. Still, they have a Tim Hortons, a nice Visitor Centre with mementos for tourists, and a decent library. If you’re in YK, stop by”

extraPins.name: Barren Ground Coffee
extraPins.caption: “Really delicious coffee, roasted locally in the NWT. Love supporting a local business, especially when the drip coffee is so good.”

extraPins.name: Houcine's Your Independent Grocer Yellowknife 50th Ave
extraPins.location: 4802 Franklin Ave #14, Yellowknife, NT X1A 1C4, Canada
extraPins.caption: “A very full supermarket, with slightly higher prices, though nothing unreasonable considering the remoteness of the location. If you’re visiting Yellowknife from another country, there’s a few Canadian touristic products for you to buy as gift or souvenirs”

extraPins.name: YK Centre Clock
extraPins.caption: “If you give me a clock, I’m going to need to take a picture with the high score, or rather the low score in this case. It was -32° here, but -39° on the trip (Hay River Beach at sunrise)”

extraPins.name: United Nations Tank Display
extraPins.caption: “You seriously don’t expect to see a UN Tank in Canada, but this one appears to have been abandoned here, and was fully covered in snow when I visited”

extraPins.name: Legislative Assembly of the Northwest Territories
extraPins.location: 4570 48 St, Yellowknife, NT NT X1A 3A5, Canada
extraPins.caption: “One of the more impressive city hall buildings that I’ve ever seen in my travels, as there’s a giant polar bear skin laying on the floor intimidatingly, and a huge Zinc wall behind the main dais”

extraPins.name: North of 60° Mining Memorial
extraPins.caption: “A fairly simple monument, but an elegant looking one at that. May they rest in Peace, indeed”

extraPins.name: Museum Restaurant by Sundog
extraPins.caption: “I visited the Heritage Centre first thing in the morning, before I’d eaten breakfast, and so I stopped at Sundog more out of convenience than intention. Regardless, I really enjoyed the breakfast sandwich and potatoes that I had here.”

extraPins.name: Prince of Wales Northern Heritage Centre
extraPins.caption: “One of my favorite attractions in Yellowknife, and the larger NWT, this museum both tells the history of the region and the historical people, and displays a lot of art and culture of the locals that call this far northern region home. …”

extraPins.name: Ceremonial Circle
extraPins.caption: “An attraction, of sorts. There’s a pathway of all the regional flags connecting City Hall from the Heritage Center and Legislative Assembly, along the body of water”

extraPins.name: United in Celebration sculpture
extraPins.location: Sombe K'e Civic Plaza, 4910 52 St, Yellowknife, NT X0E, Canada
extraPins.caption: “This sculpture depicts two people dancing in shadow with shields (?) in their hands, and is situated right at the water’s edge, though in winter it’s a bit hard to tell.”

extraPins.name: Somba K'e Civic Plaza
extraPins.caption: “In wintertime, there’s not a ton here, but for a large tree and the United in Celebration sculpture, and a ton of wind and cold”

extraPins.name: Yellowknife City Hall
extraPins.caption: “While the building was closed when I visited (on a Sunday morning), I did enjoy exploring the surrounding area and its sparse art. If you’re hoping to use the building to warm up, plan to go elsewhere”

extraPins.name: Javaroma Gourmet Coffee & Tea
extraPins.location: 5201 Franklin Ave, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3S9, Canada
extraPins.caption: “Javaroma is the (only) Yellowknife local chain, with a few locations scattered around the northern capital city. The coffee isn’t incredible, as is typical with most chains, but I really appreciate that they opened early on the weekends. They also had some fancy looking pastries”

extraPins.name: Budget Car & Truck Rental
extraPins.location: 20 Airport Road, Yellowknife, NT X1A 3T2, Canada
extraPins.caption: “Don’t be afraid of the slightly scary sign posted outside of the closed airport location, someone most likely is on the way to meet you at your reservation time. …”

extraPins.name: Yellowknife Airport
extraPins.location: 100 Idaa Rd, Yellowknife, NT NT X1A 3T2, Canada
extraPins.caption: “In terms of tiny airports in remote places of the globe, Yellowknife Airport is decently well equipped and serviced! I also believe that this is the only airport with a life sized polar bear in the main terminal, but I’ll have to keep …”

extraPins.name: Loco Pez
extraPins.caption: “Loco Pez makes a pretty good burrito, which made for a really sizable lunch”

extraPins.name: Rowhome Coffee - Front Street
extraPins.caption: “Rowhome Coffee makes their Breakfast Sandwiches on Pretzels! How ingenious! The Sausage, Egg, and Cheese ones were delicious and served piping hot. The coffee was fine”

extraPins.name: Fishtown Beverage
extraPins.caption: “Fishtown Beverage may not have the most square footage, but they occupy the space that they have quite well. That includes a really sizable refrigerated section.”

extraPins.name: Wawa
extraPins.caption: “This Wawa is perfectly fine. They have the normal menu and selection, and they have a perfectly fine gas station, but their ordering is very slow, and they forget about online orders. Make sure to check in often to make sure they’re working on your food and/or drinks.”

extraPins.name: Gilda
extraPins.caption: “Gilda is a small coffee shop and bakery, but wow do they pack a mighty punch. You can get a drip coffee to stay, and they’ll give you refills, and the pastries are simply out-of-this-world. I’ll have to come back and try the rest of the menu.”

extraPins.name: ReAnimator Coffee - Fishtown
extraPins.caption: “ReAnimator’s a neighborhood coffee spot, but with its central location, it really serves as the hub/heart of the local neighborhood. I like their drip coffee”

extraPins.name: Caletta
extraPins.caption: “Caletta is the bar area of Bastia / Hotel Anna and Bel, and it’s an intimate, lovely spot to stop for a more elevated drink and snack inside of the fancy hotel. …”

extraPins.name: Philly Halal Gyro
extraPins.location: Aramingo Avenue &, E York St, Philadelphia, PA 19125
extraPins.caption: “An extremely reasonably priced food truck, serving Halal Food. I liked the Chicken Over Rice, but it was a bit heavy on the hot sauce. I’ll go a bit lighter next time, and may try another meat.”

extraPins.name: Pet Supplies Plus Fishtown
extraPins.caption: “A very well-stocked pet store, with the largest section catering to dogs, followed by cats, and finally fish. I just wish the cat section were a bit larger.”

extraPins.name: The Richmond Shops IGA
extraPins.caption: “A neighborhood grocer with a decent selection of fresh produce, meat, and baked goods. They got all of the national brands, as well as a number of store brands, across products”

extraPins.name: Pennsylvania Railroad World War II Memorial
extraPins.location: William H. Gray III 30th Street Station, 2955 Market St, Philadelphia, PA 19104
extraPins.caption: “The signature artwork of 30th St: a humongous statue of an angel holding a fallen man on a pedestal, lined with the names of the fallen.”

extraPins.name: Amtrak Philadelphia Train Station
extraPins.caption: “30th St Station serves both Amtrak and SEPTA, and thus serves as Southeastern PA’s main connector to the region and to the whole Mid-Atlantic area. …”

extraPins.name: The Mall
extraPins.caption: “There are two interconnected green lawns on Carnegie Mellon’s main campus: The Cut, extending to Forbes, and The Mall, with its iconic shot extended out to Pitt’s Cathedral of Learning.”

extraPins.name: The Fence
extraPins.caption: “The most iconic landmark on Carnegie Mellon’s campus. The Fence has strict rules, it can only be painted by hand and by brush (no rollers), and it can only be painted after midnight. To hold The Fence, you need to keep two (or more) people …”

extraPins.name: The Bride of Penn Ave
extraPins.caption: “A hauntingly beautiful painting of the Penn Ave of Pittsburgh yester. Maybe we’ll get back there one day”

extraPins.name: Pittsburgh Glass Center
extraPins.caption: “Pittsburgh Glass Center is a combination studio space and teaching studio, where you can take classes to learn the craft of glassblowing. The studio had an exhibit filled with the students’ art, and it was simply exceptional; with some …”

extraPins.name: Friendship Perk & Brew
extraPins.caption: “Friendship Perk & Brew is local coffee shop and sit-down breakfast restaurant has a very homey feel, with some ok java and good pastries.”

extraPins.name: täkō
extraPins.caption:
“A hip and modern taqueria offering a diversity of elevated tacos in a smaller dark multilevel bar
room. The eponymous Tako taco is their speciality, and while it’s very good, it’s not my favorite.”

extraPins.name: Gates Center for Computer Science
extraPins.location: Gates Center for Computer Science, 5000 Forbes Ave, Pittsburgh, PA 15213
extraPins.caption: “Built when the Foundation was still called the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, the building’s most notable feature is the Guggenheim-esque spiral staircase that oh so slowly snakes down the mainly vertical building.”

extraPins.name: The Cut
extraPins.caption: “The Cut is the nickname for the central lawn that goes from Forbes Avenue to Hunt Library, including the Fence. I’ve always believed that it’s named that because you need to “cut” across it to get to the other half of the buildings”

extraPins.name: Walking to the Sky
extraPins.caption: “Walking to the Sky is one of the more prominent artworks on Carnegie Mellon’s campus, maybe second only to The Fence. That being said, I, among many other alums (and I’m sure current day students), really don’t love it.”

extraPins.name: Google Pittsburgh
extraPins.caption: “When you search “affordable living” on the internal search engine, it sends you to the Pittsburgh office’s page. …”

extraPins.name: Bakery Square
extraPins.caption: “Bakery Square is a shopping and building complex with a few parking garages, gyms, restaurants and corporate offices. Many of the photos included are from Google Pittsburgh, which is located across two of the buildings here, and includes an employee (and their guest) exclusive cafe.”

extraPins.name: Back Creek Books
extraPins.caption: “This store has quite the collection of rare and eclectic books. Though the store isn’t especially expansive, there were half a dozen cabinets each with a dozen unique books.”

extraPins.name: Colonial Annapolis Historic District
extraPins.caption: “Colonial Annapolis is a historic cobblestone area, with a number of notable events in its distant history. Today it’s a lovely shopping area, albeit a bit touristy, with tons of Navy men and women around.”

extraPins.name: State House Cannon
extraPins.caption: “The cannon looks a bit rough, but it’s had quite the storied history, immortalized with a plaque on it. The thing is mounted on the State House hill, point outwards.”

extraPins.name: The Annapolis Pottery
extraPins.caption: “An Annapolis institution that I’ve been visiting for my whole life. Rooms upon rooms of every kind of pottery for every use that you can think of, and a few more. If you’re visiting Annapolis for a day trip, perusing this pottery is a must.”

extraPins.name: Baron Johann de Kalb
extraPins.caption: “Located on the westside of the State House, de Kalb is standing shaking his fist to the sky. He really embodies the great energy of the capitol grounds.”

extraPins.name: Maryland State House
extraPins.caption: “Annapolis is a town built around a hill by the water, with the State House perched atop the mound. That means that you can see this magnificent building from nearly the whole of Annapolis. In the spring the cherry blossoms really add to the aesthetic. There’s a few statues and a cannon on the grounds”

extraPins.name: William Preston Lane Jr. Memorial Bay Bridge
extraPins.caption: “The Chesapeake Bay Bridge truly is an impressive bridge to traverse because of its length and various segments with their distinct regions. If you’re afraid of heights, looking around may give you a trippy sensation”

extraPins.name: Passing Through mural
extraPins.caption: “An extremely difficult mural to capture from Amtrak, as you need to be sitting on the right side on a southbound train to/through Philadelphia”

extraPins.name: Galaxy Park
extraPins.caption: “A cute little triangular cement park with a globe of sorts in the middle of a fountain. The nicest thing about this very non-green park is the surrounds”

extraPins.name: The Liberty, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Boston
extraPins.caption: “Stayed here for a work event, and the hotel itself was extremely beautiful, I heard it used to be a jail. My room was in the main building, which seemed to be unique among my coworkers, regardless I really enjoyed my room and my stay.”

extraPins.name: Viale
extraPins.caption: “A lovely place for dinner that can accommodate large parties. I really enjoyed the oysters, the octopus, and the steak when I came here for a work event.”

extraPins.name: Google Cambridge
extraPins.caption: “A lovely office comprised of three towers, connected across most floors in a very confusing manner. If you’re not a local, prepare to get lost at least once”

extraPins.name: CVS
extraPins.caption: “A fine CVS. They had a decent enough selection, but locking up deodorant is beyond excessive”

extraPins.name: GetGo Gas Station
extraPins.caption: “A fine enough gas station; the prices weren’t too egregious (all things considered)”

extraPins.name: Jenny Globe
extraPins.caption: “There aren’t a ton of notable sights as you cross Pennsylvania on the Turnpike, but the Jenny Globe certainly is one of them.”

extraPins.name: CAVA
extraPins.location: 1751 Wilmington Pike Ste B-1, Glen Mills, PA 19342
extraPins.caption: “CAVA is a fast-casual chain which makes middle eastern style food for a reasonable price. I liked the Greek Salad, though the hummus (substituted for tzatziki) wasn’t incredible.”

extraPins.name: Masamoto Asian Grill & Sushi Bar
extraPins.caption: “Masmoto is a higher end sushi restaurant with a broader array of Asian entrees. We tried a bit of everything, and it was all good! The Sashimi Platter was especially well plated, and all of the fish was extremely fresh. …”

extraPins.name: Booths Corner Collectibles
extraPins.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
extraPins.caption: “I absolutely love this stand at Booths Corner, these are my go-to movie guys, and it seems like every week they’ve replenished their wares of movies. The best part is that you’re getting them for $1, an unheard of price in America today! You can’t even rent a movie for that low”

extraPins.name: Booths Corner Arcade
extraPins.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
extraPins.caption: “There’s an arcade inside of the Booths Corner Farmer’s Market! It’s not incredibly large or fancy, but there’s a small room’s worth of games, including a few pinball games”

extraPins.name: The Club SFO
extraPins.location: San Francisco International Airport, Harvey Milk Terminal 1, International Terminal Departures Level, San Francisco, CA 94128
extraPins.caption: “There’s a Priority Pass lounge in Terminal 1 now! The Club does something close to a 1-in, 1-out system for entry, which makes sense as there’s a fixed amount of seating, and food and drink are app based which requires delivery to a …”

extraPins.name: San Franpsycho
extraPins.location: San Francisco International Airport, HARVEY MILK TERMINAL 1, San Francisco, CA 94128
extraPins.caption: “A local SF brand with fun apparel they make honoring the Bay Area, especially the city. You see them at a lot of neighborhoods’ farmers markets, and now in SFO”

extraPins.name: Wagon Wheel Barbeque
extraPins.caption: “My rule with barbecue is typically that I don’t eat it unless I can see smoke coming out of the place, and while that wasn’t the case with Wagon Wheel, I did really enjoy all of the things I tried there”

extraPins.name: Google PLYM1625
extraPins.caption: “There’s a ton of the recent Android OS figurines on the roof of this building (which is only accessible to employees and their guests). I really enjoyed taking a work call of the Android 13 swing.”

extraPins.name: Concordville Town Centre
extraPins.caption: “A decent little shopping complex with a few restaurants, big box stores, and a bank or two.”

extraPins.name: Bronze Lyricist - By Bruce Hasson
extraPins.location: 1842 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
extraPins.caption: “The statue isn’t too far back from the road, and is quite aesthetically pleasing. It’s unfortunately covered in some rusted bird poop stains”

extraPins.name: The Orb
extraPins.location: 292 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
extraPins.caption: “I can appreciate an abstract piece of art. It’s fun to walk through it and look up at the various openings. At night, the structure is lit up with bright and changing colors”

extraPins.name: The Ameswell Hotel
extraPins.caption: “My work held a happy hour / dinner event at The Ameswell Hotel, and it was great. The place has a good vibe, and the fire pits were a hot attraction as the sun set. The inside bar is very cool as well”

extraPins.name: Google Mountain View - Bay View
extraPins.location: 100 Bay Vw Dr, Mountain View, CA 94043
extraPins.caption: “One of the newer Googleplex campuses, with a bird’s nest looking building, large security gates, and an exotic interior filled with giant sculptures and newer amenities.”

extraPins.name: Google Bay View 4
extraPins.location: 400 Bay Vw Dr GSuites, Mountain View, CA 94043
extraPins.caption: “These are the Google dorm/hotels, which are only for employees. And while the location is extremely convenient for visiting Googlers going to the eastern portion of the MTV campus, I really didn’t love the rooms themselves”

extraPins.name: Wells Coffee Tarpon River
extraPins.caption: “Wells Coffee has a delicious drip coffee”

extraPins.name: MAASS Restaurant at The Four Seasons
extraPins.location: 525 N Fort Lauderdale Beach Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33304
extraPins.caption: “MAASS has a Michelin star, and from the moment that you’re seated, you can clearly see why. I had a fantastic brunch here, and while everything was excellent, the pancake was really the standout of the meal. I’ve been thinking about that sweet stack of cakes for much of the last month.”

extraPins.name: Shell
extraPins.caption: “If you’re headed back to PA, and you have ¾ of a tank or less, stop here and get the cheaper DE gas before you go home”

extraPins.name: The Shoppes at The Guitar Hotel
extraPins.caption: “There’s a very high-end mall located within the Guitar Hotel is shopping is more of your vice”

extraPins.name: The Guitar Hotel at Seminole Hard Rock
extraPins.caption: “A visually stunning landmark, and as this hotel is the largest thing in the very flat area, you can see it from miles away. A great place to go for a bit of a walk, whether you’re staying or not”

extraPins.name: Seminole Hard Rock Hotel & Casino
extraPins.caption: “The Seminole Hard Rock Hotel is such a Fort Lauderdale (area) establishment that you can see the giant guitar and its (2010s 3rd act) skybeam as you land at the airport. …”

extraPins.name: Las Vegas Cuban Cuisine
extraPins.caption: “Absolutely delicious Cuban food, with really large portions and reasonable prices. I liked my margarita (though there were no choices: frozen or shaken, or flavors), and of all the dishes, I felt that the Yuca fries were the absolute best item we ordered”

extraPins.name: the seed. Coffee + Juice Bar
extraPins.caption: “A hip coffee shop with an outdoor dining area. I really enjoyed their drip coffee”

extraPins.name: Beach Pavilion at Lauderdale-By-The-Sea
extraPins.caption: “The aesthetic facade which frames the beach. There’s spots here to sit, in a less sandy spot, and the foot wash stations are here”

extraPins.name: Lauderdale-by-the-Sea Beach
extraPins.caption: “An exceptionally beautiful beach, which wasn’t too crowded and felt like it was largely locals. You do need to park a bit inland and walk down to the shore, but once you’re there, there’s plenty of places to grab lunch, a drink, or some coffee just off the beach”

extraPins.name: Publix Super Market at Dixie Crossing
extraPins.location: 950 E Commercial Blvd, Oakland Park, FL 33334
extraPins.caption: “They make a decent chicken hoagie, with a ton of fried chicken on it”

extraPins.name: Fort Lauderdale Fire and Safety Museum, Inc.
extraPins.location: 1022 W Las Olas Blvd, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33312
extraPins.caption: “The museum was shut when I walked by in the morning, but I still enjoyed seeing everything the museum has to offer on the exterior”

extraPins.name: SE 11th Ave Swing Bridge
extraPins.caption: “When in use by cars, the 11th Ave Bridge looks completely normal. But when a ship arrives, the bridge swings itself to get out of the way, a sight to behold”

extraPins.name: Major William Lauderdale Park
extraPins.caption: “For such a small park, the Major William Lauderdale Park sure does pack a mighty punch. You get not one, but two, plaques, and a fair share of funky faced birds”

extraPins.name: Sailboat Bend Preserve
extraPins.caption: “The whole grass waterfront portion of Sailboat Bend is just a lovely place to go for a walk and admire the houses and the canal”

extraPins.name: Flanigan's Seafood Bar and Grill
extraPins.caption: “Flanigan’s is a South Florida staple, and their green plastic cups are iconic to anyone who knows the local chain. Swing by and try the dolphin (not real dolphin meat), or the ribs, or the wings”

extraPins.name: Cirque du Soleil Luzia Miami
extraPins.caption: “All Cirque du Soleil shows are spectacular, and Luzia was no different! A truly artistic and immersive experience, it was a must see while you’re in the area. All of the performers were excellent”

extraPins.name: Pegasus and Dragon
extraPins.location: 901 S Federal Hwy, Hallandale Beach, FL 33009
extraPins.caption: “A gigantic statue which is brightly lit up at night. You’ll pass by the statue if you’re going to the circus, or the mall complex.”

extraPins.name: Ann Norton Sculpture Gardens
extraPins.location: 253 Barcelona Rd, West Palm Beach, FL 33401
extraPins.caption: “Oops, all Picassos! The Ann Norton Sculpture Gardens are a bit of a misnomer, as the terrific sculptures unfortunately can’t hold a candle to all of the Picassos that they’ve accumulated in the house. They’re simply stunning, and they’ve got works across a variety of forms from the famed artist”

extraPins.name: 7-Eleven
extraPins.location: 301 Southern Blvd, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
extraPins.caption: “What a let down! From the outside, this 7-Eleven is so singular and elevated. But from the inside, there’s nothing special about this, and the fancier area is entirely obscured and you can’t go into the glass room. Don’t bother stopping if the outside beckons”

extraPins.name: Southern Boulevard Bridge Parking
extraPins.caption: “If you’re trying to get a view of Mar-a-Lago, this is the best place to see it, from across the bay. It’s easiest to get to this parking lot by turning around and heading back from Palm Beach Island”

extraPins.name: Valen Grounds
extraPins.location: 3065 S Dixie Hwy, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
extraPins.caption: “Delicious drip coffee, which was comparatively cheap.”

extraPins.name: It's All Greek
extraPins.location: 522 Belvedere Rd, West Palm Beach, FL 33405
extraPins.caption: “In an extremely pricey neighborhood, It’s All Greek has a wide menu with a variety of reasonably priced dishes. The Greek Salad was large and very fresh, and the chicken was well cooked and flavorful”

extraPins.name: Isamu Noguchi - Intetra
extraPins.caption: “An interestingly geometric statue which is set at the end of The Four Arts’ avenue, and overlooks West Palm Beach across the short waterway”

extraPins.name: Garden Club of Palm Beach
extraPins.location: 2 Four Arts Plaza, Palm Beach, FL 33480
extraPins.caption: “This was the only portion of The Society of the Four Arts building complex that I was able to explore, and I found these gardens lovely. The area isn’t huge (when the rest of the gardens are shut), but you do get a few unique gardens from around the world to walk around, including a Japanese one.”

extraPins.name: Philip Hulitar Sculpture Garden
extraPins.caption: “Wasn’t open when I came by, as some private event was being held there later that night. Still, the security people kept changing their rules to stop me from even looking into the main area. What a disappointment the staff here were”

extraPins.name: The Society of the Four Arts
extraPins.location: 100 Four Arts Plaza, Palm Beach, FL 33480
extraPins.caption: “A lovely little aesthetic building, complete with Roman style paintings at the entrance, and an elaborate, worldwide-inspired garden around the back. …”

extraPins.name: Worth Avenue Clock Tower
extraPins.location: 423 S Ocean Blvd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
extraPins.caption: “While the Worth Avenue Clock Tower is quite the simple structure, its location in front of the crystal blue waters makes it quite the spot to take a beautiful photo. Unfortunately, in 2026 this means that you’re going to have a lot of people doing endless, influencer-style photoshoots there.”

extraPins.name: The Breakers Palm Beach
extraPins.location: 1 S County Rd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
extraPins.caption: “A magnificently stunning hotel, located right on the Atlantic Ocean side of Palm Beach Island. Even if you’re not staying at the hotel, you can explore the grounds and see the impressive building and the lovely beach. You can walk from here to the Flagler museum, directly across the island”

extraPins.name: Historic Kapok Tree
extraPins.location: 315 Chapel Hill Rd, Palm Beach, FL 33480
extraPins.caption: “Admittedly, even as someone that seldom appreciates trees, this Kapok tree was quite impressive. Almost the starfish of trees, if I may”

extraPins.name: Flagler Museum
extraPins.caption: “An exceptionally beautiful state home from a generation long gone. This house has everything from elaborate statues to an entire train car inside. When you’re on Palm Beach with some time to spare, visiting the Flagler Museum isn’t a bad way to spend it.”

extraPins.name: Chik Monk
extraPins.location: 229 Sunrise Ave Ste C-5, Palm Beach, FL 33480
extraPins.caption: “The drip coffee was decent, but it felt a bit pricey (that may just be PBI!)”

extraPins.name: McDonald's
extraPins.location: 1630 S Federal Hwy, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33316
extraPins.caption: “This McDonalds has one of the old school neon signs, with the golden arch.”

extraPins.name: KUBO Asian fusion and bar -Ft. lauderdale
extraPins.caption: “A Japanese restaurant with very modern designs and stylings, that has some very good sushi. They also do events where they serve an entire tuna, which seems like a true delight”

extraPins.name: Cooley's Landing Marina
extraPins.caption: “A nice spot to walk around, within the largely Sailboat Bend living area. There’s a plaque to a past tragedy, and an abundance of birds, amongst all of the boats”

extraPins.name: Downtown Ft Laud - Laspada's Hoagies
extraPins.location: 1495 SE 17th St D, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33316
extraPins.caption: “Delicious and gigantic hoagies, which are made to order, including slicing the meat for each order. The sandwich makers also love to throw the meat from the cutter onto the bread, which is beyond amusing. Greatly enjoyed the Italian”

extraPins.name: Fort Lauderdale-Hollywood International Airport
extraPins.caption: “Not the greatest airport, but this one supports a few areas of southern Florida, from Miami to Palm Beach (though both of those places have their own airports as well). No Priority Pass lounges, but a bunch of character”

extraPins.name: LaGuardia Airport
extraPins.caption: “While not the best airport in the country, much less the world, LaGuardia is most likely the best major airport supporting the NYC area. There’s a lot of lounges, including a Priority Pass-accepting Chase Lounge, and a good selection of …”

extraPins.name: Phillies Mural
extraPins.caption: “What a great recent addition to the east bank of the Schuylkill River, which you can see as you drive into Center City on 76.”

extraPins.name: Stephen's On State
extraPins.caption: “A fine place for dinner! Stephen’s On State has been a staple of State St. for my whole memorable life, but somehow I’ve waited more than 30 years to show up.”

extraPins.name: PetSmart
extraPins.caption: “It’s a rather sizable PetSmart with a decent selection of cat, dog, bird, fish, and smaller animal supplies. They also have a fairly large number of animals housed inside”

extraPins.name: Wawa
extraPins.caption: “Not the largest Wawa, but it functions great in a pinch on the way to Philly, and has all the essentials.”

extraPins.name: Chase Sapphire Lounge by The Club PHL
extraPins.location: Philadelphia International Airport, Terminal D/E, 8500 Essington Ave, Philadelphia, PA 19153
extraPins.caption: “The Chase Sapphire Lounge is a lovely addition to the Philly airport, with its large square footage, fancier food options, and full, complimentary drink menu. …”

extraPins.name: Tipsy Putt
extraPins.caption: “Came here for a work event, and it was fine. The food wasn’t excellent (Mexican-ish), and the games were fun enough!”

extraPins.name: Satkar
extraPins.location: 1253 W El Camino Real, Sunnyvale, CA 94087
extraPins.caption: “A vegetarian Indian restaurant in South Bay. As someone that doesn’t eat (much) dairy, it was a tiny bit of a challenge to order here, but so many of the dishes can be made vegan, which really helped. The food was all great, and the portions were large”

extraPins.name: Sports Page
extraPins.caption: “The Google bar, Building 50, B50 (it’s not a private bar). There’s trivia and a sand volleyball court and tvs in the back. …”

extraPins.name: Udon Mugizo
extraPins.caption: “I’m so glad that I found Udon Mugizo because my dinner was excellent. I wanted tsukemen and they recommended the Tempura Zaru Udon, which was close enough and simply delicious. …”

extraPins.name: Google Gradient Canopy
extraPins.location: 2000 N Shoreline Blvd, Mountain View, CA 94043
extraPins.caption: “One of the newest Google buildings, which is inaccessible even to most of the employees who work on the larger Mountain View campus, because of the teams that sit inside”

extraPins.name: Haze Dispensary
extraPins.caption: “A fine shop, they had a decent supply and a bunch of first time discounts.”

extraPins.name: Aloft by Marriott Mountain View
extraPins.location: 840 E El Camino Real, Mountain View, CA 94040
extraPins.caption: “A nice and convenient place to stay while on a business trip to Mountain View. I was able to check-in at 1:50am without any hassle (I did call ahead and warn that my plane was extremely delayed).”

extraPins.name: Duck Wall
extraPins.caption: “There are small eccentric pieces of San Francisco which make me love this city, and Duck Wall is absolutely one of them. What wonderful weird art”

extraPins.name: The Painted Ladies
extraPins.caption: “There’s a good argument to be had about where to find the nicest sunrise in SF, and Alamo Square Park, overlooking The Painted Ladies, must be near the top of any list. You can see the downtown skyscrapers of the Financial District from the park’s perch, and ships beyond in the Bay.”

extraPins.name: Alamo Square Park
extraPins.caption: “Beautiful views overlooking downtown. The famous Painted Ladies are located on one leg of this park, which features the downtown skyscrapers behind it. Alamo Square Park is a lovely place to take in a sunrise”

extraPins.name: Sightglass Coffee
extraPins.caption: “Some of the best coffee in the city. Never made a bad drink, and they sell some of my favorite roast beans in the Bay Area”

extraPins.name: Rock Spinner and Hopscotch
extraPins.caption: “Though this area, at the end of Lawton St, isn’t quite as nice at the Sunset Dunes park area at Newton, there’s still a giant octopus, Lands End mural on the ground, and a truly imposing rock stood upright between the lanes.”

extraPins.name: Sunset Dunes
extraPins.caption: “I’m so happy that SF voted to transform this portion of the road to a permanent park. It’s a beautiful space along the ocean, open to everyone”

extraPins.name: Lands End Lookout
extraPins.location: 680 Point Lobos Ave, San Francisco, CA 94121
extraPins.caption: “The area with all the groovy trees above Sutro Baths, which wraps around a good part of the way into the Bay towards the Golden Gate Bridge. This is one of my favorite parts of the city, I love walking through the trees, and taking in the ocean air. But be wary, it can get cold up there.”

extraPins.name: SFO Rental Car Center
extraPins.location: 780 N McDonnell Rd, San Francisco, CA 94128
extraPins.caption: “Apart from being located quite far aware from the airport, the SFO Rental Car Center is quite nice, has a large garage, and a decent variety of companies supported here. …”

extraPins.name: SFO Museum Gallery Harvey Milk Terminal 1
extraPins.location: San Francisco International Airport, 8097, San Francisco, CA 94128
extraPins.caption: “Not the largest gallery space, but there’s a few displays in a dark (and not incredibly inviting) hallway, next to Ritual coffee. It’s worth a quick visit, but certainly not worth risking missing your flight to see”

extraPins.name: Bun Mee SFO Terminal 3
extraPins.location: San Francisco International Airport, Food Hub, Domestic Terminals Departures Level Terminal 3, San Francisco, CA 94128
extraPins.caption: “It’s a really nice looking shop, they’re quite fast, and they’ve got nearly their whole menu from their SF locations. Unfortunately, the food is a hearty step down from the city locations.”

extraPins.name: San Francisco International Airport
extraPins.caption: “Caveated by this being my home airport, this is absolutely the best airport in the country. Most of the terminals are connected on the inside. If you have TSA Precheck, waits are never longer than 10minutes, and usually only a few people. …”

extraPins.name: Philadelphia International Airport
extraPins.caption: “While I’m not the biggest fan of PHL, I’ll admit that the airport has gotten quite the facelift in the past few years, and is now about as good as most of the major US airports. …”

extraPins.name: TJ's Grill N Chill
extraPins.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
extraPins.caption: “A great, reasonably-priced, neighborhood greasy spoon spot for breakfast and lunch eats. The Meat Omelette had a ton of scrapple, and was very hearty for the price - the Home Fries were likewise great. The only downside is that breakfast ends at 1pm.”

extraPins.name: Dos Gringos Mexican Kitchen
extraPins.caption: “I enjoyed the Tacos Mexicanos with Pork Carnitas from Dos Gringos. If you dine-in, they give you some warm, fresh (tasting) tortilla chips and salsa, and the verde was mild but nicely flavorful. …”

extraPins.name: La Buona Cucina
extraPins.location: 1362 Naamans Creek Rd, Garnet Valley, PA 19060
extraPins.caption: “Delicious prepackaged Italian meals, which you can freeze to make last longer.”

extraPins.name: Dante West Village
extraPins.caption: “I came to Dante with a party of 20 for a large work event, and they had customized the menu for us, which was pretty unique and a very nice touch. Then the food was absolutely delicious, the chicken was so well cooked, but really everything …”

extraPins.name: M&M'S New York
extraPins.caption: “The M&M store in Times Square is something of a tourist attraction, as there’s mascots, apparel, and signage recognizing the prominent location, but if you’re not trying to buy some chocolate or a souvenir, there’s little to see or do”

extraPins.name: Chelsea Market
extraPins.caption: “A block-long food market with a wide variety of permanent vendors, and a mix of other shops. There’s often some cool displays detailing older NYC of years past, and to the history of the building, which was once a biscuit factory.”

extraPins.name: Grand Bazaar NYC
extraPins.caption: “A weekly market with dozens of vendors arranged in a tennis court, expanding into a high school gymnasium. There were mainly clothing, goods, and art stands, with a food section by the entrance and free Vitamin Water samples.”

extraPins.name: The Viand
extraPins.caption: “While The Viand isn’t an old-school NYC diner, they still get the job done when you’re in need of a breakfast. They’ve got quite large omelettes for a fair price, which come with homemade jam. The coffee was fine”

extraPins.name: Gray's Papaya
extraPins.caption:
“Gray’s Papaya is an institution of the Upper West
Side, most notably for their hot dogs and their papaya juice, but they also sell quite tasty breakfast sandwiches which are only $3 with a cup of coffee. …”

extraPins.name: AMC 84th Street 6
extraPins.caption: “One of the smaller AMC theatres in the city, and while they don’t have any larger format screens here (no IMAX or Dolby), they do have the fancy recliners; so you get comfort over the visual resolution.”

extraPins.name: 7th Street Burger Upper West Side
extraPins.caption: “A good place to stop and get a good, greasy smash burger and some fries. The burgers were better than the fries, and same as with Five Guys, you’ll likely want to get a double if you’re an adult. …”

extraPins.name: El Gallo Taqueria
extraPins.caption: “An option for pretty solid Mexican food for a rather reasonable price  The Carne Asada bowl was decent, and I really like their tacos, with the Carne Asada being a bit better than the Al Pastor”

extraPins.name: Chopt Creative Salad Co.
extraPins.location: Moynihan Train Hall Food Court, 383 W 31st St Ste 037, New York, NY 10001
extraPins.caption: “A great option for a lunch on the go. The salads were reasonably priced and extremely portable. I’d definitely recommend the Greek Salad and adding Chicken, you also get free bread.”

extraPins.name: The Met Cloisters
extraPins.location: 99 Margaret Corbin Dr, New York, NY 10040
extraPins.caption: “The Met Cloisters is situated atop a hill at the very tippy top of Manhattan, and serves as something of a prize for venturing up to the sleepier portion of the island. …”

extraPins.name: Superfly New York City - Upper West Side Licensed Adult-Use Recreational Dispensary
extraPins.caption: “A decent dispensary with a wide selection, and a slightly higher price point. It looks fancy inside, and they’ve got machines where you can view their products.”

extraPins.name: The Strand
extraPins.caption: “Some book stores have this calming ambiance and The Strand has that in heaps. An extremely expansive bookstore with a children’s section in the basement.”

extraPins.name: Brickman's Columbus Ave
extraPins.caption: “An extremely densely packed hardware store that’s likely got what you’re looking for. There were a number of employees ready to help me as well.”

extraPins.name: Crumbl Cookies
extraPins.caption: “The national gourmet, giant cookie and cake chain. Their desserts are good, but certainly more of a treat, or a gift, than a regular item. …”

extraPins.name: Moynihan Food Hall
extraPins.caption: “The Moynihan Food Hall (within Penn Station) has a surprisingly wide selection of restaurants to choose from before you catch your train.”

extraPins.name: Broad Nosh Bagels
extraPins.caption: “One of the better bagel options in the UWS, though don’t get the salt bagel. It was entirely covered in rock salt and way overly done. …”

extraPins.name: Spring St
extraPins.caption: “A decent station. Nothing fancy, and nothing artsy, but it gets the job done. There’s an underpass to get to the other direction trains.”

extraPins.name: 7 Hudson Square
extraPins.caption: “7 Hudson Square is the new home of Disney in New York, both the corporate offices, and the studio spaces living within the building. In the mornings, you can see celebrities entering and exiting the building for their media obligations, and upstairs there’s a theatre for employee only screenings, and a Starbucks”

extraPins.name: Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis Reservoir
extraPins.caption: “The Reservoir is the largest body of water in Central Park and one of its most notable landmarks. You can’t go out onto the water, and you certainly can’t swim in it. There is a running track that goes along the perimeter of the body of water, which enforces a single direction of traffic, counter-clockwise.”

extraPins.name: The Lake
extraPins.location: Central Park, Bow Bridge, New York, NY 10024
extraPins.caption: “There’s a few bodies of water within Central Park and The Lake is one of the more prominent ones, although not the largest. But for The Pond, it’s the most downtown body of water, so it gives some of the best reflected skyscraper views. You can also see the Dakota and other iconic UWS buildings from here.”

extraPins.name: St. Paul the Apostle Church
extraPins.caption: “New York City has no shortage of beautiful churches, but St. Paul the Apostle stands out in that crowded field. Not only does it have a brilliant facade, it has a stunningly colorful, cavernous interior. I could’ve spent hours here studying every detail, this building is truly a work of art.”

extraPins.name: Swingers NoMad
extraPins.caption: “A very expansive, indoor miniature golf place, with multiple courses located on the property. It’s a very aesthetically pleasing place, with colorful lights, and good scenes for photography. They also have decent food and drinks. I came here for a work event and we all had a great time”

extraPins.name: Imagine Mosaic
extraPins.location: Imagine, Terrace Dr, New York, NY 10023
extraPins.caption: “The Upper West Side has its own little, micro Times Square in the former of a tribute to a former Beatle. This is one of the few, rare places that you’ll spot a crowd in the quieter neighborhood, and plenty of vendors hocking their wares, and musicians busking famous Lennon tracks.”

extraPins.name: Times Square Diner & Grill
extraPins.caption: “I was trying to get brunch somewhere else in the neighborhood, but they were crowded, so I came to the Times Square Diner and they were fine. The Strawberry Nutella Pancakes were really the standout, with the omelettes and home fries both just being fine. I didn’t love the coffee.”

extraPins.name: Peace Fountain by Greg Wyatt
extraPins.caption: “The Peace Fountain may be my singular favorite statue in the whole of New York City. There’s so much going on, it’s chaotic, it’s messy, it’s fantastic. It’s surrounded by a ring of smaller animal statues, complimenting the animal parts that encompass the larger artwork.”

extraPins.name: H&H Bagels
extraPins.location: Moynihan Train Hall, 421 8th Ave, New York, NY 10199
extraPins.caption: “The H&H in Penn Station is located between the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall and the Food Court, and while there’s often a line, it does move quickly. This is a fair place to grab a breakfast before heading on your train, or a black and white cookie as a gift.”

extraPins.name: City Diner
extraPins.caption: “A large square-footage diner with a bar counter, an old timey feel, and some good pancakes. A friend and I got two Egg dishes (an Omelette and Eggs), and an order of Chocolate Chip Pancakes, and the cakes were by far the standout. Also didn’t love the house coffee.”

extraPins.name: Tom's Restaurant
extraPins.caption: “Let’s be real, you’re not coming to Tom’s for the food, you’re coming here because of the show. And while Tom’s certainly caters to the fans by having a number of pictures of the cast, it’s functionally just a typical NYC diner. The Lumberjack was pretty decent”

extraPins.name: Kossar's Bagels & Bialys
extraPins.caption: “Kossar’s makes an excellent breakfast sandwich, I went with my typical Sausage, Egg, and Cheese on an Everything Bagel, and I loved what I got. They brew La Colombe coffee, and my only complaint is that their cups are horrible; it still leaked through two cups”

extraPins.name: Hall of Saurischian Dinosaurs
extraPins.caption: “One of my favorite parts of the History Museum, filled with Dinosaurs stretching across vast halls, and towering over crowds. But be wary, this is also one of the busiest parts of the building, with a heavy density of people filling every nook and cranny.”

extraPins.name: Horace Greeley Monument
extraPins.location: 894-900 Ave Of The Amer, New York, NY 10001
extraPins.caption: “Horace has the misfortune of having both an old looking face and an old sounding name. At least they gave the old guy a chair to spend eternity in. They’ve also surrendered him with flowers, making the whole thing look almost like a tomb. RIP Ol’ Horace”

extraPins.name: Carl Schurz Park
extraPins.location: East 86th Street &, East End Ave, New York, NY 10028
extraPins.caption: “Carl Schurz Park is located on the East River in the Upper East Side, and contains a section of John Finley walk and Gracie Mansion. There’s also a Peter Pan Statue and a lot of green shrubbery, it’s a fine place to go for a break or a bit of a walk.”

extraPins.name: Penn Station
extraPins.caption: “NY Penn Station has a worse reputation than it deserves. As someone that regularly uses Amtrak, I really like the aesthetic design of the station, the availability of the subways underneath, and the selection of restaurants and shops and their hours.”

extraPins.name: Schmackary's
extraPins.caption: “Somehow NYC has a bunch of competing gourmet cookie chains. Schmackary’s is a delicious offering, with more reasonably sized cookies, which were all named after Broadway shows. I got the Book of Mormon one, which was great. I’ll be back to try more.”

extraPins.name: The Ravine
extraPins.caption: “There’s a few areas of Central Park where you can get deep enough into the green to forget that you’re still in the heart of the largest city in the country. The Ravine is one of those places, which makes it one of my favorite parts of the megacity”

extraPins.name: Eleanor Roosevelt Memorial
extraPins.caption: “Eleanor Roosevelt was the first female aviatrix to fly across the Pacific Ocean, until everything changed when she vanished one day from her house never to be seen again. People have searched everywhere for her plane, but no one knows where it went”

extraPins.name: Läderach
extraPins.caption: “A gourmet chocolatier with a higher price point which makes decent gifts for loved ones. The store has a human-sized statue of liberty made out of chocolate inside, and heaps of sheets of chocolate. They also tend to give out free samples as well.”

extraPins.name: Sutton Park
extraPins.caption: “There’s really three attractions in Sutton Park, first the stunning views of the Queensboro Bridge. Then there’s quite a nice statue to a boar in a greener portion of the park. And finally, there’s the views of the Eastern portions of the city.”

extraPins.name: Morningside Park
extraPins.caption: “While not as famous as Central Park or Riverside Park, Morningside Park is one of Manhattans great parks. Located above Central Park on the westside, this park offers a number of steep, hilly paths, and a serene lake with a purported waterfall.”

extraPins.name: Times Square
extraPins.caption: “Times Square is arguably the most famous place in New York City, and in turn, maybe the most consistently busy. There’s a ton to see, from people watching, to taking in the thousands of neon adverts blaring, there’s much to see in Times Square”

extraPins.name: Apthorp Cleaners
extraPins.caption: “Apthorp Cleaners have some of the most elaborate storefront windows that I’ve seen on the UWS. The current two are Barbie and Wicked: For Good, and there’s easily a dozen dolls in each with custom backgrounds and floors, arranged into scenes.”

extraPins.name: Porto Rico Importing Co.
extraPins.caption: “One of the best smelling shops in NYC, with endless burlap sacks full of roast coffee beans, and their beans are largely quite good. There’s staff that can walk you through choosing the right beans for your tastes, and they also have all of …”

extraPins.name: Central Park
extraPins.caption: “NYC’s iconic park, and one of the largest urban parks in the world, Central Park is the home to multiple bodies of water, horse stables, and fantastic views of the large residential buildings that line the sides, and skyscrapers at its base.”

extraPins.name: Inwood Hill Park
extraPins.location: Payson Ave. &, Seaman Ave, New York, NY 10034
extraPins.caption: “If you’re looking for the furthest north point in Manhattan, you’ve found it! Inwood Hill Park sits at the northwest corner of the island, and is equally dense with trees and sparse with humans (on the ground). Though you can nearly always …”

extraPins.name: Gracie Mansion Conservancy
extraPins.location: 181 East End Ave, New York, NY 10128
extraPins.caption: “Honestly, I didn’t realize that Gracie Mansion was located here when I was intending to see Peter Pan, but this was something of a nice surprise. You really can’t get up close to the building at all, which makes sense, for security purposes.”

extraPins.name: Carnegie Hall
extraPins.location: 57th Street and, 7th Ave, New York, NY 10019
extraPins.caption: “Carnegie Hall is one of the preeminent concert venues in the country, if not the world, and you can almost feel the grandeur in the halls. I was lucky enough to see Gustavo Dudamel conduct Tosca here, and will certainly try to return soon”

extraPins.name: Google NYC - Chelsea Market
extraPins.caption: “Google purchased the entirety of the historic Chelsea Market building more than a decade ago, and while the public floors haven’t been updated, the upper (employee only) floors are really quite exquisite, and one of the more interesting …”

extraPins.name: Bareburger
extraPins.caption: “I really enjoyed Bareburger, they’re a slightly more elevated NYC burger chain, with a bit of a higher price point, which gets you a higher quality burger, with more fun accoutrements. It’s also a sit down restaurant, which caught me by …”

extraPins.name: Non-Violence - Carl Fredrik Reuterswärd
extraPins.location: United Nations Secretariat Building, 405 E 42nd St, New York, NY 10017
extraPins.caption: “I’m certain Non-Violence is a better statue than I’ve reviewed it, but it’s so inaccessible from the street, it’s a true shame. Art shouldn’t be hidden behind walls, and I’d assume the UN (of all organizations) that should understand that”

extraPins.name: Just Salad
extraPins.caption: “Great salads, and they come with free rosemary-y bread. They have a whole array of precurated options, and you can swap out any ingredients that you want. Just Salad also has a rewards program in you get their app, or go on the website. …”

extraPins.name: 190 St
extraPins.caption: “Quite an interesting metro station. The signage at the upper level is cool and retro, however you have to take an elevator down from there. There’s another entrance, at the ground level, but no stairs or escalators to get you down there”

extraPins.name: Mount Tom
extraPins.caption: “Less of a mountain and more of a big honking rock, you can climb Mount Tom and get a decent overview of the Warsaw Monument, but on account of the heavy tree cover, not much else. Still, it’s a fun place to do a bit of rock scrambling.”

extraPins.name: Church of the Heavenly Rest
extraPins.caption: “An exceptionally stunning single-halled church. Cast with white stone calls, and elaborate stained glass panels lining three of the side, the Church of the Heavenly Rest exudes beauty from every pew and from under each and every arch.”

extraPins.name: St. Frances Cabrini Shrine
extraPins.location: 701 Fort Washington Ave, New York, NY 10040
extraPins.caption: “St. Frances Cabrini Shrine is a church, so if you’re visiting on a Sunday, there will be services going on. There was a front area with a gift shop-appearing section, that was cool even if I didn’t get to see the rest of the building”

extraPins.name: General Grant National Memorial
extraPins.location: W 122nd St &, Riverside Dr, New York, NY 10027
extraPins.caption: “The General Grant Memorial has a few unique things going for it. Maybe most notable is the mosaic bench that stretches around the perimeter of the building. Closely followed by Grant’s tomb which is just a bit north of the building.”

extraPins.name: American Museum of Natural History
extraPins.location: 200 Central Prk W, New York, NY 10024
extraPins.caption: “Certainly one of the best Natural History Museums in the country, if not the world. Regardless of which animal, vegetable, or mineral you’re hoping to see, it’s likely in this museum. My favorite exhibits were the butterflies, the …”

extraPins.name: Blue Bottle Coffee
extraPins.caption: “When you’re in Penn Station and need a quick cup of coffee, or a pastry, Blue Bottle isn’t a bad option. They’re situated right in the main atrium of the Moynihan Train Hall, which is super convenient for those commuting via train.”
